channel.title: Elias Sorel · new works
channel.description: Open preprints by Elias Sorel (French, with English abstracts) on the living world, matter and the cosmos. Each work has a DOI on Zenodo.

item.title: The mitochondrion, complexity as a debt rather than a conquest (Endosymbiosis · Bioenergetics · Eukaryogenesis), version 3
item.dc:creator: Elias Sorel
item.description: Almost every one of our cells hosts a former bacterium. It has kept its own DNA, bacterial-type ribosomes, a double membrane, a respiratory chain and, in many protists, its old bacterial machinery for dividing in two. This essay does not ask whether it gave us a gift. It asks what its case forces us to undo: the story of a conquered complexity. In one sentence, complex life would not be a summit climbed, but the inheritance of an entry, a bacterium kept alive inside another cell, whose dependence the whole lineage has carried ever since. Part by part. THESIS · It came in: a single entry for all known eukaryotes, dated between 2.37 and 1.80 billion years ago (Kay et al. 2026) and tested on 1,399 proteins (Záhonová et al. 2026); a host already organised (Eme et al. 2023; Imachi et al. 2026); the cousinhood, its family of living bacteria (Rickettsia, Pelagibacter, Wolbachia, Midichloria); only 14 to 16% of its proteome traces back to the bacterium (Gabaldón and Huynen 2004, 2007). ANTITHESIS · And yet the engine is contested: the bioenergetic thesis of Lane and Martin (2010) against Lynch and Marinov (2015), and the state of the controversy (Gerlitz et al. 2018). SYNTHESIS · It stayed: from partner to organelle; mitochondrial DNA still moving into the nucleus (66,083 human genomes, Wei et al. 2022); the only established complete loss (oxymonads); and a stress test, what if oxygen disappeared. A falsifiable prediction closes the text. Three registers are kept apart: ESTABLISHED, DEBATED, READING. 8 figures, 105 references with DOI. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22918398

item.title: The mantis shrimp: the eye that seeks attunement (Fist · Eye · Attunement)
item.dc:creator: Elias Sorel
item.description: The mantis shrimp is known for its strike: a club launched at up to 23 m/s, hitting twice, the second time through a collapsing cavitation bubble. This text starts from that fist and moves to the eye: up to 16 photoreceptor classes, a living quarter-wave retarder, and yet poor colour discrimination. Proposed reading: an eye that rolls on itself acts as a rotating analyser, and mantis shrimp vision may be a search for attunement rather than a fine image. 78 references, 9 testable questions. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23891659

item.title: The Equation of the Self: a journey through the individual (Free Will · Imbalance · Self)
item.dc:creator: Elias Sorel
item.description: L'Équation du soi (The Equation of the Self) poses the self as an equation to be tested in chemistry, physics and mathematics, not as a definition: a bath of 29 molecules, an I recognised only through a you, a we measured as phase agreement. 35 equation boxes, 11 proposed tests, 218 references. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23858442

item.title: The Diamond: what vibrates, remembers, illuminates (Vibration · Memory · Light)
item.dc:creator: Elias Sorel
item.description: Le Diamant (The Diamond) follows one question across three levels: are rest, conservation and perception what they appear to be? I · Vibration (thesis): nothing is at rest. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22730664

item.title: The Icosahedron: what layers, is read, resonates (Scale · Perception · Resonance)
item.dc:creator: Elias Sorel
item.description: This text starts from a question: from which scale do we look at the living world? It holds in one sentence, "life is a recommencement at different scales", and measures it in three parts. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23250209
